case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses a Bluetooth qualification issue involving inter-layer inconsistency between GAP (Host) and LL (Controller) due to mismatched Channel Sounding (CS) support. The customer attempts to use a newer SDK-based Host Design while keeping an existing Controller Design. The consultant explains why standard combinations fail due to ICS inconsistencies and explores alternative Design Numbers. Ultimately, a workaround using 'Combine Unmodified Designs' is proposed to complete qualification without additional testing.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main issue is an inter-layer dependency (ILD) inconsistency caused by mismatched CS support between Core-Host and Core-Controller Designs. Even when using subset Designs, inherited ICS flags (e.g., CS-related GAP items) can remain enabled, causing inconsistency. The Qualification Workspace consistency check prevents combining such mismatched Designs under normal new Design creation. Additionally, the availability of CS-disabled Host Designs for a specific SDK version is limited, constraining valid combinations. The discussion highlights how ICS inheritance and Design Number limitations affect qualification feasibility.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant determines that the inconsistency cannot be resolved through normal Design selection because no suitable CS-disabled Host Design exists for the desired SDK version. Since modifying ICS would require creating a new Design and potentially trigger testing, the fallback is to use 'Combine Unmodified Designs'. This option bypasses ICS modification and consistency enforcement, allowing reuse of existing Designs as-is. The key logic is that qualification validity is preserved because both Designs are already qualified, even if their combination has inherited inconsistencies.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer attempts to create a new Design with inconsistent ICS, the submission will fail the consistency check and block qualification. Trying to force a fix by modifying ICS could trigger new testing requirements, increasing cost and schedule. Selecting an incorrect Design combination may also lead to repeated submission failures and delays. Additionally, unnecessary testing could be incurred if the reuse path is not properly utilized.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When inter-layer inconsistencies cannot be resolved due to limitations in available Design Numbers or inherited ICS constraints, using 'Combine Unmodified Designs' can be a valid fallback to complete qualification without additional testing, provided all referenced Designs are already qualified.
